messages:
Lina: Heads-up: MerchantOne signed a 6-month enterprise commit. They want a "production-like" load test during holiday promo windows. Peak target: 600 QPS chat, avg 130 tokens in / 220 out (350 total). Embeddings are 8%. They requested recommended reserved GPUs, a burst/autoscale plan, preheat strategy (edge-prefetch + KV), and quick security bullets for procurement. Start date: Jun 10.

Omar: Quick clarifiers: are peaks sustained (minutes)? p95 output length? preferred model family?

Lina: Peaks ~4-8 minutes during promo. Most flows are chat (92%); model preference is 13B quant for baseline, optional fallback to a 50B distilled variant only if quality tests require it. They care about consistent checkout latency under 350ms p95.

Elliot: Ballpark sizing math:
```
peak_qps = 600
tokens_per_req = 350
tokens_per_sec = 210000 t/s
assume_13B_quant = 50k t/s per GPU -> 210k/50k = 4.2 -> 5 GPUs
assume_50B_distill = 18k t/s per GPU -> 210k/18k = 11.7 -> 12 GPUs
```
Recommend baseline commit = 5 GPUs (13B). Allow burst to 8 GPUs (3 extra) for headroom and warmup. If they demand 50B at peak, call out high-cost scenario (~12 GPUs).

Ravi: Autoscale proposal: min_reserved_pool = 3, commit_reserve = 5, burst_limit = 3 (max 8), scale_step = 1 GPU, cooldown = 90s. Routing: send to reserved pool first; if queued requests > 120 or reserved utilization > 90% then spin burst slot. If burst capacity exhausted, apply graceful queueing with 429/503 and a short retry-after. Prewarm: run edge-prefetch to populate top-100 prefixes into KV and allocate 1 prewarm slot 2h before promo.

Omar: Operational notes: prefix KV cache will reduce decode token load for returning sessions by ~20-30%. Recommend persistent KV cache enabled, and a 2-phase warmup: 1) 4h background warm cache job for top customers; 2) 30m targeted preheat for highest traffic prefixes right before promo. Also set embeddings batching aggressively (max_tokens=8192) since embeddings are small pct.

Elliot: Pricing ballpark for presales: reserved_gpu_month ~= "$5.5k" per GPU (13B-equivalent). Burst on-demand ~= "1.6x" reserved. So commit 5 GPUs => ~$27.5k/mo baseline. Bursting 3 GPUs continuously would add a prorated premium (~$26k/mo if used fully) but expected burst usage is intermittent so prorated cost much lower. Mark finance to confirm final numbers and discount tiers.

Lina: Security/procurement bullets they asked for: data residency, SOC2/pen-test, KMS/CMK support, audit logs, BAA.

Ravi: Short answers for packet: 1) EU/US regions available for data residency; 2) SOC2 Type II and penetration test summary available on request; 3) Customer-managed keys supported in Private/VPC; hosted can integrate CMK options on request (some limitations); 4) Audit logs retained 90 days by default, extended retention available as add-on; 5) BAA feasible but needs legal review (typical 5-10 business days). Note: HSM-backed KMS or encryption-in-use requested -> requires Private deployment and network prep (lead time ~2-4 weeks).

Elliot: Reliability guardrails: canary rollout 10% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% across 48 hours with automated rollback if p95 latency > 1.2x baseline for >5 minutes or error rate spike >0.5%. Add dashboard widgets: tokens/sec by pool, queue length, p50/p95/p99 latencies, model fallback counts.

infra-bot: preheat-scheduler: edge-prefetch job scheduled for 2024-06-09T20:00Z (top-100 prefixes, duration 4h), and targeted 30m preheat for top-10 customers at 2024-06-10T09:00Z.

Lina: Action items:
- Elliot: produce one-pager (sizing table, sensitivity by seq-length and KV hit-rate, cost delta reserved vs burst)  due EOD tomorrow
- Ravi: ops runbook + preheat checklist + canary steps  draft by tomorrow 9am PT
- Omar: loop finance for precise pricing and discounts; provide per-GPU monthly/rate card
- Lina: assemble SOW snippet and procurement packet, send to customer by COB

Omar: ack. Elliot: ack. Ravi: ack. Lina: thanks team, will attach one-pager to deal and request token-length histogram from MerchantOne if they can share.
